claim.pdf_says: where locale-phrase-1 is:  followed by a vertical stack enclosed in a single tall brace pair: locae-name-1 / LOCALE / SYSTEM-DEFAULT / USER-DEFAULT, with LOCALE, SYSTEM-DEFAULT and USER-DEFAULT each underlined (required words). Same structure for locale-phrase-2 with locale-name-2.
claim.why_it_matters: These two sub-figures are the only diagrams on the twelve pages that are paraphrased into prose plus a bullet list instead of being drawn like their siblings. The bullet form does not record that LOCALE, SYSTEM-DEFAULT and USER-DEFAULT are underlined (required words) whereas locale-name-1 is a user-defined word, and it does not state the brace semantics (exactly one alternative shall be selected). Nothing is contradicted, but the required-word marking the rest of the transcription preserves is absent.

verdict.reasoning: REFUTED. Rendered specs page 315 at 300 dpi (printed folio 285, 12.3.6 OBJECT-COMPUTER paragraph) and cropped both sub-figures to ~2x. What the printed page actually shows is confirmed: each 'where locale-phrase-N is:' sub-figure is a four-line vertical stack inside ONE tall brace pair; the first line is a lowercase user-defined word (locae-name-1 / locale-name-2) with NO underline, and LOCALE, SYSTEM-DEFAULT and USER-DEFAULT each carry a visible underline rule. So the claim's reading of the PDF is accurate. The claim nevertheless fails on all three of its own grounds. (1) CONTENT IS FULLY PRESERVED: the markdown lists all four alternatives, in the printed top-to-bottom order, for BOTH sub-figures, and explicitly identifies the construct as a brace group. Nothing is added, dropped, reordered, renamed or contradicted; the residual difference is purely presentational (prose + bullets vs. ASCII brace art), which is an explicit rejection criterion. (2) 'DOES NOT STATE THE BRACE SEMANTICS' IS FALSE: the transcription writes 'A brace group containing:', naming the standard's own convention, and 5.2.6.3 Braces -- transcribed verbatim in the same markdown file -- supplies the semantics ('the syntax element contained within the braces or one of the alternatives contained within the braces shall be explicitly specified or is implicitly selected'). A drawn brace would convey exactly this and no more. (3) THE UNDERLINE PREMISE IS FACTUALLY WRONG: the claim asserts the bullet form drops 'the required-word marking the rest of the transcription preserves'. It does not preserve it. This transcription NEVER encodes underlines inside a fenced code block; underlines are recorded only in an optional prose 'Figure notes' block (215 such blocks, 180 'are underlined in the printed standard' sentences), and the directly comparable pure-reserved-word brace stacks carry no underline note at all -- e.g. encoding-phrase (BINARY-ENCODING / DECIMAL-ENCODING) and endianness-phrase (HIGH-ORDER-LEFT / HIGH-ORDER-RIGHT) at md lines 13365-13375, and the 13-way category-name stack at 27554+. Drawing the locale-phrase stacks as brace art would therefore have carried exactly as much underline information as the bullets do: none. The required/optional distinction is also not recoverable-relevant here, since each reserved word is the SOLE token of its alternative, so a non-underlined reading would produce an empty alternative; and lowercase-hyphenated vs. UPPERCASE already marks user-defined vs. reserved per 5.2.6.1. The claim is a style-uniformity observation ('these two are the only ones not drawn' -- true: 'A brace group containing' occurs exactly twice in the whole 2.96 MB transcription), not a content discrepancy, and it changes no meaning. INCIDENTAL, NOT CLAIMED: the PDF genuinely misprints the first alternative of locale-phrase-1 as 'locae-name-1' (missing the l) where the markdown prints 'locale-name-1'. That is a silent and correct normalization of an obvious ISO typographical defect -- syntax rule 3) on the same page prints 'Locale-name-1', and locale-phrase-2 prints 'locale-name-2' -- it is not the divergence the claim alleges (the claim quotes the typo without flagging it), and it does not change meaning either.
verdict.corrected_description: No correction warranted -- the claim is rejected rather than restated. The only glyph-level divergence found on the page is unclaimed and benign: the PDF misprints 'locae-name-1' (dropped l) in the locale-phrase-1 brace stack and the markdown silently normalizes it to 'locale-name-1', consistent with syntax rule 3) on the same page and with locale-phrase-2. If the reconciliation wants the two locale-phrase sub-figures redrawn as brace art for uniformity with encoding-phrase/endianness-phrase/category-name, that is a cosmetic house-style cleanup, not a transcription error, and it would not by itself add any underline information the rest of the transcription carries.
